logline: One night on the Vigil, the verse rises early — and the bill goes to the man standing next to her.
spine: A tide-caller takes an ordinary watch, finds the water a hand-span wrong, and puts it back. She has done this a hundred times and it has never cost her much, and she has never once asked why not. Eleven minutes to make an audience notice the thing she has spent a career not noticing.

acts.title: Dusk · the watch
acts.summary: Maren alone on the rail. The tables say neap; the water disagrees. Establish the ledger, the six columns, and the tithe-box at the north gate that nobody looks at twice.

acts.title: Bells · the correction
acts.summary: Bells a night early. She calls the tide back a hand-span at a time. Bray on the stair, filling the wait with a story. The call works and she is barely winded — which is the wrong reaction, and the film must let it sit.

acts.title: Slack water · the rupture
acts.summary: Bray mishears her. Once, slightly, and he laughs it off. She does not. Then the Chorister on the rail, not looking at her — looking toward the town — with the only line the film needed: *the last verse. listen the other way.* Cut before she can follow the look. We do not subtitle the song.
